newsitem.title: UK: Lure in Mocatta sale would be a seat at gold fix.
newsitem.headline: Lure in Mocatta sale would be a seat at gold fix.

text.p: News that Standard Chartered Plc subsidiaries Mocatta Base Metals and Mocatta Bullion are to merge fuelled speculation on Monday that the combined unit may soon be for sale.
"The seat at the fixing would be the cachet," said a bullion market source, discussing the potential attraction to a buyer of the Mocatta name.
Founded in 1671, the firm is the oldest member of the panel that conducts the twice-daily London gold price fixing.

Standard Chartered was, however, unwilling to comment on a report in the Sunday Telegraph which said it did not consider the metals and gold trading divisions "part of its core business" and it was willing to sell for around $200 million.

The base metals group employs 57 staff for 380 customers and operates in 40 countries. Mocatta is a ring dealing member of the London Metal Exchange under Standard Chartered Bank flag and is rated in top five of the world's base metals traders.
The bullion unit employs 130 staff serving 800 customers.
"The two were merged because a lot of customers overlap and it was logical to join them," a Standard Chartered spokesman said. "There is not that much scope for (staff cuts)," he added.
But gold market insiders had few doubts that offers would be considered.
"Let's put it this way, if Standard Chartered sold it, they wouldn't be sorry," said one market insider.
Mocatta - formerly Mocatta and Goldschmid - is a market making member of the London Bullion Market Association and one the five houses taking part in the London gold fix.
It is also the oldest member of the London gold market having been founded in 1671. For 121 years from 1720 it acted as the exclusive broker in gold and silver to the Bank of England.

A buyer would have to be approved by the Bank of England, as the supervisor of the gold market, and after a previous round of takeovers involving fixing houses in the early 1990 it might be hard to please.
Market sources said that with three members of the fixing already owned by non-British banks and one (N.M. Rothschild) independent, another foreign owner might not be welcome.
But another market insider said the Bank of England would approve a significant bank regardless of its origin.
A Bank of England spokesman had nothing to say.
"What we could be looking for (as a buyer) is an established member of the London Bullion Market Association which does not have a seat at the fixing," a bullion source said.
Other bullion and metals market sources noted that the pace of "downsizing", desk mergers and relocating business units had gathered notably in the past few weeks.
Rothschild recently announced it was relocating its Singapore bullion desk to an established unit in Sydney.
Last week AIG International Inc announced its gold trading desk in Hong Kong would shift to the United States, most likely before the end of 1996.

Lehman Brothers in New York earlier this year announced cuts on its bullion department in New York and other companies have either merged bullion and base metals or made cuts as bullion prices have remianed depressed in a narrow trading band.
"It adds up to an overwhelming overcapacity. And with spreads as thin as they are, some people must be losing money," one market analyst said.
